notes: Architecture determinism self-check. Ran on AMD EPYC 7513 (the earlier RUN-0052 preflight ran on Intel Xeon Silver 4310). Two independent captures on the SAME node compare 21 files, 0 differ -> SELFCHECK_DETERMINISTIC_OK: the solver is bit-deterministic on cluster hardware. The same capture vs the committed baseline gives 21 files, 18 differ, and the EPYC values are bit-identical to the Xeon values from RUN-0052 (e.g. direct/fit_sensor_rmse 0.0009213998644646732 on both), so all x86_64 nodes agree with each other and only the arm64 baseline differs. Exit code is nonzero only because the script reports the baseline comparison after the self-check; the self-check itself passed. Root cause: results/solver-regression/before was captured on Apple M2 (arm64, NEON); the cluster is x86_64 with OpenBLAS DYNAMIC_ARCH (AVX-512 capable), and the two reassociate floating-point sums differently. Confirmed by building a local venv at the locked numpy 2.5.3 and rerunning the gate on arm64: 21 files compared, 0 differ. So the lockfile and numpy are NOT the cause; CPU architecture is. No tolerance was loosened.
